correctness.rationale: Every double derivation in a contranominal context is the identity, so minimized extents are exactly finite-poset minima. This yields the antichain characterization and singleton consequence difference by direct set algebra. The strict-consequence generating function follows from enumerating subsets containing a strict predecessor; its polynomial basis identifies predecessor-count multiplicities. Pairwise tests recover strict comparison, while two explicit star orders with matching minima for all residual sets of size at least three prove optimality. The five-point collision is checked both by a short Hasse-cover invariant and exhaustive script, and the three-point orientation gap is explicit. A standalone cross-check enumerated all 4473 labeled posets through size five and 139062 premises; these are finite support, not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The foundational 2024 theory explicitly asks about information linking typical concepts and nonmonotonic conditionals. This theorem gives a complete structural answer in its simplest Boolean testbed: typical extents forget orientations, a polynomial retains the predecessor-degree distribution, and pairwise residual conditionals reconstruct every comparison at an optimal premise size. The five-point collision shows the polynomial plus all typical concepts still cannot reconstruct the order. This natural comparison is not an arbitrary finite parameter statistic; it identifies concrete recoverability limits for preference-driven concept compression.
